newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia approves 5.41 bln rgt foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia approves 5.41 bln rgt foreign investment.

text.p: Malaysia has approved 5.41 billion ringgit ($2.06 billion) in foreign investment in the first six months of 1997, International Trade and Industry minister Rafidah Aziz said on Tuesday.

She told a briefing on the annual Malaysia International Trade and Industry Report 1996/97 that a total investment of 12.6 billion ringgit was approved between January and June 1997, with 43 percent coming from foreign investors.
That compares with 34.26 billion ringgit in approved investment projects for all of 1996, of which 17.06 billion ringgit came from foreign sources, according to figures in the annual report.
In 1995, total investment was 20.87 billion of which 9.1 billion came from foreign sources.
The top six foreign investors in 1996 were Singapore, Japan, the United States, Switzerland, Taiwan and South Korea, the report said.

Singapore's investments increased almost five-fold to 4.8 billion ringgit from 1.1 billion in 1995. Japanese investments increased 120 percent to 4.6 billion from 2.1 billion and U.S. investments rose 61 percent to 2.9 billion ringgit.
The bulk of foreign investment -- 9.2 billion ringgit or 54 percent of the total in 1996 -- was in the electrical and electronics sector, which accounts for two-thirds of Malaysia's total exports.
Malaysia's investment overseas in 1996 amounted to 6.8 billion ringgit. Singapore was the top destination with 1.7 billion ringgit followed by the United States with 1.0 billion.
From 1987 to December 31, 1996 Malaysia had approved 7,846 investment projects with total proposed investment of 203.8 billion ringgit, 65 percent of which has been implemented.
A further quarter was in the initial stages of implementation and 10 percent had not got off the ground, the report said.
